chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Do not tire of reciting 'When the earth is shaken with its shaking', for whoever recites it in his optional prayers, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not strike him with an earthquake ever, nor will he die by it, nor by a thunderbolt, nor by a calamity from the calamities of the world until he dies.

And when he dies, a noble Angel descends upon him from his Lord and sits by his head, and says: 'O Angel of Death, be kind to the friend of Allah, for he frequently remembered me and mentioned the recitation of this Chapter.'

And the Chapter says to him similarly, and the Angel of Death says: 'My Lord has commanded me to listen to him and obey, and not to extract his soul until he instructs me with that. So when he instructs me, I will extract his soul.'

And the Angel of Death does not cease to be with him until he instructs him with the extraction of his soul; and when the cover is lifted for him, so he sees his stations in Paradise, so he extracts his soul from the gentlest of what can be from the treatment. Then his soul is escorted to Paradise by seventy thousand Angels, hastening with it to Paradise.

key_terms.إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ: When the earth is shaken (opening of Surah Al-Zalzalah)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and protections promised for reciting Surah Al-Zalzalah in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the spiritual efficacy of Surah Al-Zalzalah, often recited in the second rak'ah of Fajr, linking its frequent recitation to divine protection from sudden calamities (al-zalazil). It elaborates on the concept of 'tadkhul al-mawt' (ease of death), where the Surah itself acts as an intercessor alongside the Angel of Death, ensuring the believer's soul is extracted gently and escorted by a multitude of angels, reflecting the high status of the 'Wali Allah'.
